# GitHub Orb frame animation

## Scope and preferences

Use this project's offline Three.js renderer, not image-pose crossfades, for Copilot and Mona. Keep motion calm and readable on a 2.1-inch display. Maintain Copilot image/vector fallbacks and Mona's own procedural cat-eared fallback, never substitute Copilot artwork for Mona. Do not change session aggregation, observer behavior or GitHub polling for visual changes. The detailed Copilot guidance below remains Copilot-specific; do not impose its eye rig or materials on Mona.

## Source and rights

The source is `martinwoodward/octoprints`, `models/copilot/copilot_multicolor.3mf`. This is a print mesh, not a rigged character. `media/copilot/source.json` records the exact revision and attribution; `media/copilot/LICENSE.txt` retains CC BY-NC 4.0. Preserve attribution, identify adaptations, and do not imply GitHub affiliation. Commercial distribution requires separate permission. Do not assume GitHub trademark permissions from the copyright license.

The 3MF contains one mesh with Bambu triangle paint values `4`, `8`, and `0C`. The preparation script rejects unfamiliar split-paint encodings instead of guessing. Raw geometry uses Z-up and faces negative Y; rotate X by minus pi/2 for Three.js. Separate painted regions into shell, blue trim, dark face, and emissive eyes. The eye mesh is centered on its own pivot so blinking does not move the whole head.

Use `tools/model-regions.ts` to identify the three connected paint-8 regions: face panel and two lenses. Do not use triangle-centroid height cutoffs for goggles; they create sawtooth material boundaries and misclassify the upper face. Blend rim colors per vertex using surface distance to the lens boundaries. Compute normals on the welded whole mesh before splitting materials, and give each lens its own UV bounds. Keep lens highlights dark and stable rather than relying on bright specular lighting.

### Mona source and bounded display adaptation

Read `tools/MONA.md`, `media/mona/source.json`, `tools/mona-model.ts`, `tools/mona-motion.ts`, `tools/mona-scene.ts` and `tst/tools/mona.test.ts` before Mona changes. Mona comes from `models/mona/mona_multicolor.3mf` at pinned revision `981a85f0bec9d1a9c280fd5719d0d797852229c4`, the same revision as retained Copilot; acquiring it does not update Copilot. Preserve the untouched `media/mona/source.3mf`, SHA-256/provenance, `LICENSE.txt`, original paint strings, and firmware attribution to Martin Woodward and contributors. CC BY-NC 4.0 is a copyright license, not GitHub trademark permission or affiliation; commercial use/distribution requires separate permission.

Mona is also an unrigged print mesh: identity component transform, 7,498 vertices and 15,000 faces; retain print-bed placement as metadata without applying it. Rotate intrinsic Z-up/negative-Y front by -π/2 about X. Preserve violet/white/black/pink filament colors and compute welded whole-mesh normals before material separation. Seven split-painted microfaces are decoded from bounded Bambu trees (maximum depth 64), then assigned their modal filament, ties to the lowest index. This is a recorded display simplification, **not** exact paint-subdivision reconstruction. Reject truncated/unknown paint, unexpected palette/transforms/counts rather than guessing. Do not relax Copilot's distinct split-paint rejection rules.

Use deterministic whole-character gestures without face stretching or an artificial eye rig. Current Mona bounds are yaw ≤0.16, absolute pitch ≤0.09, absolute roll ≤0.15 radians, no translation or scale change. All three clips are transparent 320×320, 24-frame, 12-fps two-second one-shots; motion ends at 1.5 seconds with six stable closing frames. Preserve framing, 2560×960 atlases, 320×320 posters, and final-frame clamping.

## Files and workflow

1. Read `dashboard/motion.ts`, `tools/scene.ts`, `tools/render-frames.ts`, `dashboard/frames.ts`, and existing tests before editing.
2. Run `npm install --prefix tools` on a fresh checkout. Run `npm run prepare:model --prefix tools` only when acquiring or updating the source. It resolves the upstream revision and generates the retained model, mesh JSON, license and source metadata. Do not silently refresh the source for a motion-only change.
3. Use the original artwork in `media/images/` to tune `media/copilot/reference-look.json` and materials, camera and lighting in `tools/scene.ts`. Preserve measured reference samples separately from chosen material colors. Use lavender shell highlights, saturated blue goggles, deep navy face shading, purple lens reflections and cyan eye scanlines. Render at 2x resolution, downsample to 320 by 320 pixels and encode WebP at quality 0.98. Keep output transparent, orthographic and consistently framed. Verify cyan eyes and blue goggles in a rendered poster; do not apply a harsh sharpening filter or change the calm motion to compensate for detail.
4. Tune deterministic poses in `dashboard/motion.ts`. Motions use clip-local time, not randomness or wall-clock time. Defaults are 8-second loops at 12 fps and breathing under 0.4% scale. Thinking uses a slow upward glance and asymmetric squint; input uses a curious dog-like tilt up to 0.22 radians and wider eyes; error uses a gentle side-to-side "no" gesture up to 0.2 radians. Completion has smiling eye arches, a small 0.1-unit bounce and a softer rebound, then settles. Avoid confetti, recurring hops, rapid wobble, and large camera movement. Keep each eye on its own centered pivot.
5. Loop endpoints must match. A blink must open again before the loop boundary. One-shot clips must settle; playback holds their last frame rather than restarting them. Preserve a clear state ring independently of character motion.
6. Run `npm run render --prefix tools`. The script starts a temporary loopback server, renders using headless Chrome, and writes transparent WebP atlases, a PNG poster and a versioned manifest to `media/animations/`. It closes the browser and server afterward. On macOS it uses installed Google Chrome; otherwise use `CHROME_PATH` or install Playwright Chromium with `npx --prefix tools playwright install chromium`.
7. Run `npm test --prefix tools`, `npm test --prefix dashboard` and `npm test --prefix bridge`. With the bridge running, run `npm run verify:dashboard --prefix tools` for actual browser playback, atlas dimensions/hashes, MIME types and traversal rejection. Confirm source revision, all seven Copilot moods, Mona's four event-triggered moods over three clips, frame counts, loop wrapping, one-shot clamping, missing-asset fallback and motion bounds.
8. Restart the bridge if its static mappings changed, reload the dashboard, select **3D frame sequences**, and inspect all mood previews. Check orientation, light exposure, dark panel contrast, eye blinking, transitions, completion settling, RGB565 preview and real-size readability. Do not claim visual verification without actually viewing renders.

For Mona, run `npm run prepare:mona --prefix tools` only when acquiring the pinned source, then `npm run render:mona --prefix tools`, `npm run export:firmware --prefix tools`, `npm test --prefix tools` and `npm run verify:mona --prefix tools`. The renderer merges manifest version 1 without removing Copilot clips/provenance; Copilot rendering likewise preserves Mona. `verify:mona` checks decoded browser pixels, not a visual review. Inspect all three Mona previews, settled final poses and identity-only fallback separately. These tools do not emit bridge events or upload devices.

## Playback contract

Tool uses focused downward-looking eyes, mild working nods and an occasional small blue sweat drop that slides and fades; only Tool may show sweat. Error uses rounded cyan X eyes that persist when the no gesture settles. Inspect `media/animations/tool-poster.png` and `error-poster.png` after rendering to verify these expressions and their placement.

`manifest.json` specifies frame size, FPS, column count, per-clip frame count, looping, filename and SHA-256 digest. Atlases are row-major. `dashboard/frames.ts` crops one frame at a time; unavailable Copilot frames fall back to image artwork, then a drawn face. Baked frames must not receive the old procedural head bob and tilt again. Frame playback only changes rendering; the bridge remains the source of live state.

The Mona adapter contract from `tools/MONA.md` is `mascot: 'mona'`, `clip: 'mona-pr' | 'mona-workflow' | 'mona-security'`, integer `presentationId`, and `alert: { id, kind, title, url, repository }`. PR uses `needsInput`; workflow/security use `error`. Select by explicit clip, not shared mood; newer revisions restart, unchanged session updates do not. Identity/clip/mood transitions still apply. Mona is sticky latest news; meaningful accepted Copilot events switch back, excluding `sessionEnd`, while sessions continue underneath the masked mood. Keep that selection in the bridge, not animation tools. The dashboard draws Mona procedurally if frames are missing or image/vector mode is selected; Copilot retains image-then-vector fallback. Both clients retain mascot identity during local disconnect handling.

## ESP32 handoff

WebP atlases are development assets, not firmware-ready files. Do not load complete atlases into ESP32 RAM. Run `npm run export:firmware --prefix tools` to convert all atlas cells into independently decodable JPEG frames with 4-bit RLE alpha inside `firmware/data/animations.orb`. The pack carries clip metadata and a CRC32 per frame. Default JPEG quality is 0.82 and the exporter rejects output above 12 MiB.

The firmware reads the pack from the onboard microSD card, reads only the current frame, and uses PSRAM for its compressed payload, 100 KiB alpha plane, and RGB565 display buffers. Keep background, ring, source dots and labels outside baked frames so firmware can draw them independently. After changing animation source, render and export, then copy `animations.orb` and `ATTRIBUTION.txt` to the FAT32 SD-card root. There is no flash filesystem partition; do not use `uploadfs`. For firmware-affecting changes, follow the [firmware upload skill](../esp32-firmware-upload/SKILL.md) and upload immediately after validation. Validate pack size/CRCs and real-device frame rate; browser playback alone does not prove embedded decoder throughput or color fidelity.

Current export: **7,837,791 bytes, 10 clips, 624 frames, 320×320 at 12 fps**, including seven Copilot clips and `mona-pr`, `mona-workflow`, `mona-security`. Keep clip names within 15 characters plus NUL in the ORBA version-1 16-byte name field. Rendering/exporting alone does not transfer assets to the SD card; see `firmware/README.md` for the copy and firmware upload procedure. Missing Mona assets on firmware use the procedural Mona silhouette, not another mascot's frames.

Runtime presentation is event-triggered and mascot-specific. `protocol/emotions.json` is authoritative: each mascot mood selects an animation clip, visible task label, and ring configuration with an explicit `mode` of `animated` or `solid`. Copilot session events select Copilot moods; GitHub PR assignment/review, workflow failure, and security alerts select Mona's `prAssigned`, `reviewRequested`, `workflowFailure`, and `securityAlert` moods. The PR moods intentionally share `mona-pr` while keeping distinct task labels. Bridge snapshots resolve these fields; clients must render them rather than infer them from a shared mood name. Keep the ring outside baked animation frames.
